description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a comforting and nutritious staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. This hearty soup features tender red lentils simmered with aromatic vegetables and traditional spices, creating a rich and satisfying flavor profile. Often served with a squeeze of fresh lemon and a drizzle of olive oil, it is a perfect meal for any day.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain. Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and dice the carrot and potato into small, uniform pieces. This ensures even cooking.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and diced carrot, cooking for another 3 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine and Season
instructions.text: Stir in the rinsed red lentils, diced potato, ground cumin, and ground turmeric. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to toast the spices and coat the lentils. This step enhances the flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Achieve Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Once the lentils and vegetables are tender, remove the pot from the heat. For a smoother soup, use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup to your desired consistency. Alternatively, you can mash some of the lentils and potatoes against the side of the pot with a spoon for a thicker texture.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately with warm pita bread.

tips: For an extra layer of authentic flavor, consider making a 'ta'leeyeh' (garlic and cilantro fried in olive oil) and stirring it in at the very end.
If you prefer a thicker soup, reduce the amount of broth slightly or mash more of the lentils and potatoes. For a spicier kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the other spices.
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup tastes even better the next day as flavors meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for longer storage.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a beloved staple across the Middle East, particularly cherished in Lebanon for its comforting warmth, rich flavor, and incredible nutritional value. This humble yet hearty soup transcends seasons, offering a soothing embrace on a chilly evening and a light, nourishing meal on a warmer day. A cornerstone of Middle Eastern soups and stews, Adas embodies the essence of simple, wholesome cooking, turning basic ingredients into a culinary masterpiece that has been passed down through generations.

Packed with protein, fiber, and essential minerals, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is not only delicious but also incredibly good for you. It’s naturally vegan, gluten-free, and remarkably easy to prepare, making it a perfect choice for healthy eating and busy lifestyles. Its vibrant color, zesty lemon finish, and fragrant mint aroma make it an unforgettable dish that brings a taste of authentic Lebanese home cooking right to your table.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

At its heart, "Adas" is simply the Arabic word for lentils, and this soup celebrates the red lentil in all its glory. Unlike brown or green lentils, red lentils break down beautifully when cooked, creating a naturally thick and creamy texture without the need for any dairy or flour. Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is characterized by its bright, tangy flavor profile, primarily from generous amounts of fresh lemon juice, complemented by the aromatic punch of sautéed garlic and onion, and finished with a distinctive flourish of dried mint.

This soup is more than just a dish; it's a cultural icon. It represents the resourcefulness and culinary wisdom of Lebanese cuisine, transforming inexpensive, readily available ingredients into a dish that is both deeply satisfying and incredibly flavorful. It's often served during Ramadan for breaking the fast, as a comforting meal during winter, or simply as a nutritious lunch any day of the week. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavor that makes it universally appealing, a true testament to the power of fresh, quality ingredients.

## Ingredients for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas

The beauty of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas lies in its short and humble ingredient list, which collectively creates a symphony of flavors.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. They cook quickly and break down to create a creamy base. Ensure they are thoroughly rinsed before cooking.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Sautéed until fragrant, they provide a sweet and savory depth.
*   **Olive Oil:** A cornerstone of Mediterranean cooking, used for sautéing and as a finishing drizzle for richness and flavor.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** The liquid base. Broth adds more flavor, but water works perfectly well, especially with good seasoning.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for the characteristic bright, tangy finish that cuts through the richness of the lentils. Do not skip this!
*   **Dried Mint:** The signature herb. It adds a unique, cooling, and aromatic dimension that is quintessential to Lebanese Adas.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season and enhance all the other flavors.
*   **Optional Garnishes:** Fresh parsley or cilantro, additional lemon wedges, a swirl of extra virgin olive oil, or toasted pita bread for dipping.

These ingredients, when combined correctly, create a balanced and incredibly flavorful soup that is both nourishing and deeply satisfying.

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas

Preparing this delicious soup is surprisingly straightforward, even for novice cooks. Here’s a step-by-step guide to achieving the perfect Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas:

1.  **Rinse the Lentils:** Place your red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse them thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Combine Ingredients:** Stir in the rinsed red lentils, vegetable broth (or water), salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil.
4.  **Simmer:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Achieve Desired Consistency:** At this point, the soup will be thick and creamy. For a smoother consistency, you can use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup directly in the pot. Alternatively, carefully transfer portions to a regular blender (vent the lid!) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Some prefer a slightly chunky texture, so blending is optional based on your preference.
6.  **Finish with Lemon and Mint:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice and the dried mint. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your liking. The lemon is key, so don't be shy!

## Tips for the Best Adas Soup

To elevate your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas from good to truly exceptional, consider these tips:

*   **Fresh Lemon is Non-Negotiable:** Bottled lemon juice simply doesn't compare. Freshly squeezed lemon juice provides a bright, vibrant acidity that is essential to the authentic flavor of Adas.
*   **Don't Skimp on Olive Oil:** Use good quality extra virgin olive oil, both for cooking the aromatics and as a finishing drizzle. It adds a wonderful richness and flavor.
*   **Bloom the Dried Mint:** For an even more intense mint flavor, briefly "bloom" the dried mint. Heat a tiny amount of olive oil in a small pan, add the dried mint, and cook for about 15-30 seconds until fragrant. Stir this infused oil and mint into the soup at the very end.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. If it's too thin, let it simmer uncovered for a few more minutes to reduce slightly.
*   **Let Flavors Mingle:** Like many soups, Adas often tastes even better the next day, after the flavors have had more time to meld and deepen.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, and especially lemon juice. These final adjustments can make all the difference.

## Serving Suggestions for Red Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **As a Main Meal:** Serve a generous bowl of Adas as a light yet filling main course. A drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or cilantro, and a few lemon wedges on the side for squeezing are classic garnishes.
*   **With Bread:** It pairs perfectly with warm pita bread, crusty bread, or even toasted croutons for dipping and soaking up every last drop.
*   **As an Appetizer:** A smaller portion makes a wonderful starter to a larger Middle Eastern feast.
*   **With a Simple Salad:** Complement the soup with a fresh, crisp green salad tossed with a simple lemon-tahini or olive oil vinaigrette for a balanced meal.
*   **Add a Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of red pepper flakes or a dash of hot sauce can be added to individual servings.

## Variations & Substitutions for Adas

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas recipe is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with variations to suit your taste or available ingredients:

*   **Added Vegetables:** For extra nutrition and texture, consider adding finely diced carrots, celery, or even a small potato along with the lentils. They will soften and meld into the soup.
*   **Spice It Up:** A pinch of ground cumin or coriander can add an earthy depth. A tiny bit of turmeric can enhance the color and add a subtle flavor. For heat, a pinch of cayenne pepper or a small green chili can be added with the aromatics.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional, you can also experiment with fresh mint, fresh cilantro, or parsley stirred in at the end for a brighter, fresher flavor.
*   **Broth Alternatives:** While vegetable broth keeps it vegan, chicken broth can be used if you prefer and are not adhering to a strictly plant-based diet.
*   **Garnishes Beyond Mint:** Toasted pine nuts, finely chopped spring onions, or even a dollop of plain yogurt (if not vegan) can add interesting textures and flavors as a garnish.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a timeless dish that offers comfort, flavor, and nutrition in every spoonful. Its ease of preparation and simple ingredients make it accessible to everyone, inviting you to explore the rich and vibrant world of Middle Eastern soups and stews. Whether you're seeking a wholesome meal, a comforting bowl, or an authentic taste of Lebanon, Adas is sure to become a beloved addition to your culinary repertoire.
